evidence.claim: Fixed-asset investment rose 5.1% in 2022, with infrastructure up 9.4%, manufacturing up 9.1%, and health and social work investment rising strongly in the year-end statistical release.
evidence.locator: main results paragraph and the subsections on investment by sector
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistics release with concrete sectoral investment changes relevant to social services and productivity foundations.
evidence.period_fit: Directly reports 2022 spending and investment outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate attribution: the investment mix reflects central priorities, but actual execution depends on ministries, provinces, and state firms.
contrary_evidence: Strong investment does not automatically prove better service quality or fairness.
Private-sector performance and property-sector weakness temper the welfare interpretation.

evidence.title: Real estate development and sales in 2022
evidence.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
evidence.claim: Real estate development investment fell 10.0% in 2022; housing starts fell 39.4%; sales area fell 24.3%; and funding for developers fell 25.9%.
evidence.locator: main results paragraph in the NBS release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistics release giving exact property-sector declines for 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for national policy context, but not a single-person attribution; the downturn reflects the campaign to rein in leverage and the wider property downturn.
contrary_evidence: The figures point to a major housing-sector stress rather than a clean welfare gain.
These data alone do not show whether any households received offsetting support.

evidence.title: China created 12.06 million new urban jobs in 2022, but youth unemployment hit 16.7 percent in December
evidence.claim: China created 12.06 million new urban jobs in 2022, but the 16-24 unemployment rate reached 16.7% in December and the statistical bureau said young people faced greater hiring difficulty.
evidence.locator: lead paragraph and the December youth-unemployment sentence
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official labor-market release with specific 2022 headline outcomes and a clear downside indicator.
evidence.period_fit: Directly concerns 2022 labor-market life chances.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate attribution: job creation and youth unemployment reflect central macro-management but also property, COVID, and global-demand shocks.
contrary_evidence: Headline job creation is substantial, but youth unemployment is a serious counterweight.
Employment totals do not reveal job quality or distributional fairness.

evidence.title: After two months, a scarred Shanghai's COVID-19 lockdown ends
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Shanghai's two-month lockdown left residents frustrated and in economic loss, confined 25 million people for almost all of the lockdown, and that many struggled to get enough food or medical care.
evidence.locator: opening paragraphs beginning 'Following two months of frustration, despair and economic loss...' and 'During two months, numerous residents ... struggled to get enough food or medical care'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong independent wire service; the article gives detailed contemporaneous reporting with concrete harms.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 lockdown period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for national zero-COVID policy and its enforcement under Xi-era governance, though immediate implementation was local and municipal.
contrary_evidence: The lockdown may have reduced viral spread in the short run, which Reuters notes indirectly through the 'zero COVID' status.
A single city does not prove nationwide welfare failure.

reasons.reason: This is crisis-harm evidence about zero-COVID, not a general welfare outcome across all social domains.

evidence.title: World Report 2023: China
evidence.claim: HRW said China's strict Zero-COVID policy confined residents in Shanghai and other cities for weeks, significantly impeded access to health care, food, and other necessities, and led to reports of people dying after being denied treatment for non-COVID illnesses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: HRW is an independent monitor; the report is retrospective but specific and detailed, and aligns with other reporting on the same period.
evidence.period_fit: Covers 2022 conditions directly, though published shortly after year-end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for central policy choice and tolerance of harsh enforcement, though the report does not isolate Xi personally from the broader party-state apparatus.
contrary_evidence: HRW acknowledges the policy may have prevented some Covid deaths and illnesses.
The report is advocacy-oriented, so it benefits from corroboration with Reuters and Amnesty.

reasons.reason: Same as E0089: keep as adverse counterevidence, not as a stand-alone measure of all social policy.

evidence.title: China 2022
evidence.publisher: Amnesty International (via Amnesty Germany / ecoi mirror)
evidence.claim: Amnesty reported that strict Covid restrictions in some cases undermined the right to health and adequate food, that authorities abused the Covid health-status app to restrict movement and peaceful assembly, and that some local officials were sanctioned for manipulating the app.
evidence.locator: sections 'Recht auf Gesundheit' and the paragraph on app misuse during June 2022 protests
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Amnesty is an experienced rights monitor; the report is retrospective but specific about 2022 events and mechanisms.
evidence.period_fit: Covers the full 2022 period explicitly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for state policy under Xi and for tolerated administrative abuse; direct personal attribution is limited to the central government and party-state system.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes China later substantially relaxed restrictions on 7 December and 26 December 2022.
As an advocacy report, the strongest claims are best corroborated by other sources.

reasons.reason: This is also crisis/rights harm evidence; it should be used as a counterweight, not as a substitute for broader social-policy assessment.

evidence.title: Xi stresses full, strict Party governance, vows zero tolerance on corruption
evidence.claim: Xi vowed a zero-tolerance stance on corruption and said officials should not dare, be able, or want to become corrupt.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official state-news report of Xi's in-period speech with specific anti-corruption commitments.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to Xi's current leadership agenda.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi as his stated governance standard, but it is self-report rather than independent proof of practice.
contrary_evidence: Self-declared anti-corruption is not the same as proved personal honesty.
The same system is opaque and centrally controlled, so rhetoric may overstate practice.

reasons.reason: Xi's anti-corruption speech is self-report and aspirational, not evidence of his personal honesty.

evidence.title: Chinese Wisdom in Xi's Words: 'Strict implementation of laws leads to order'
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Justice of the PRC / Xinhua
evidence.claim: Xi called on administrative, judicial, and procuratorial organs to stop lax enforcement and take resolute action against officials who abuse power for personal gain, place power above the law, or bend the law to suit their own ends.
evidence.locator: search-result excerpt and quoted paragraph on abuse of power for personal gain
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official translation of Xi's legal-governance line, but the page was only accessible through search-snippet evidence here.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2022 and explicitly about Xi's governing principle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable as Xi's instruction to the state apparatus, though it is a norm-setting statement rather than proof of compliance.
contrary_evidence: This is a general principle, not a case-specific finding about Xi's own conduct.
It does not independently verify that abuse of power was actually prevented.

reasons.reason: Legal-governance rhetoric is norm-setting, not proof of actual conduct.

evidence.title: China tightens regulation of business activities of officials' relatives
evidence.claim: The Party Central Committee issued rules restricting officials' spouses, children, and children's spouses from certain business activities and requiring annual reporting of relatives' business activities, with false reporting punishable.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary national-policy notice with concrete conflict-of-interest rules and penalties.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong institutional attribution to Xi-era central governance; it does not by itself prove Xi's own family interests were implicated.
contrary_evidence: The policy is preventive and does not show a specific Xi-family conflict.
It shows that the system needed stronger controls, which cuts both ways.

evidence.title: Xi: Winning tough, protracted battle against corruption
evidence.claim: Xi said the anti-corruption fight must never rest, that officials must not gain the audacity, opportunity, or desire to become corrupt, and that there should be no mercy for corruption.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official report of Xi's congress speech with direct quotations.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and central to the target-year leadership record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable as Xi's own stated standard, but still self-report and not independent verification.
contrary_evidence: Anti-corruption rhetoric can also be a power-consolidation tool.
The source does not establish whether corruption claims were applied evenly.

reasons.reason: Congress anti-corruption rhetoric is self-affirming and should not be treated as independent honesty evidence.

evidence.title: Xi: CPC achieves overwhelming victory, fully consolidates gains in fight against corruption
evidence.claim: Xi said the Party had achieved an overwhelming victory in the fight against corruption, had removed serious hidden dangers in the Party, country, and military, and had used unprecedented campaigns against corrupt officials.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official transcript/report of Xi's 2022 congress address.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable as Xi's stated assessment of the system he leads, but not an independent audit.
contrary_evidence: The claim is self-congratulatory and unverified by the source itself.
It can coexist with selective enforcement and loyalty screening.

reasons.reason: Same issue: this is self-congratulatory official rhetoric, not an independent integrity finding.

evidence.title: Profile: Xi Jinping leads China on new journey
evidence.claim: Xi ordered leading officials to regularly report personal and family matters such as marriage status, personal finances, and business involvement, while the Party regulated the business involvement of more than 4,700 officials' spouses, children, and children's spouses and expanded oversight through the National Commission of Supervision.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official profile article with specific institutional mechanisms and explicit Xi directives, but it is promotional and not independent.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to his post-congress governance style.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for Xi's personal leadership of the anti-conflict/oversight system, though still not direct proof of his own finances.
contrary_evidence: The article is a celebratory profile, so it likely overstates the cleanliness of the system.
The measures target officials generally, not Xi's own household specifically.

reasons.reason: Institutional controls over officials are context, not direct proof of Xi's own personal honesty.

evidence.title: Press Center for 20th CPC National Congress: 2nd press conference
evidence.claim: The briefing said the reporting system for officials' personal matters was expanded, spot checks rose from 3-5% to 10% annually, all officials registered at and supervised by the CPC Central Committee were fully checked before the congress, and officials' relatives' business activities were put under stricter regulation.
evidence.locator: press-conference answer from Xu Qifang in the search-snippet excerpt
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official congress press briefing with specific implementation details, but the page was not directly fetchable here and the evidence comes from the search snippet.
evidence.period_fit: In-period and directly about 2022 enforcement practices.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong institutional attribution to Xi's leadership of the party discipline system, but still not a personal financial disclosure.
contrary_evidence: It shows broad surveillance of officials rather than independent scrutiny of Xi himself.
The details reflect internal compliance controls, not transparent public accountability.

reasons.reason: Internal monitoring and compliance controls are not the same as independent scrutiny of Xi himself.

evidence.title: Xi Jinping makes important speech at meeting of criticism and self-criticism of Political Bureau
evidence.claim: Xi said Political Bureau members must be strict with their family members, relatives, and people around them and must never allow them to seek illegitimate interests by taking advantage of power and influence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official reporting of Xi's in-period speech, but only the search snippet was accessible here.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and specifically about ethical conduct and family restraint.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi's own ethical standard-setting, though not evidence that he himself complied perfectly.
contrary_evidence: This is a norm-setting speech, not proof of actual restraint.
It says more about expected behavior than demonstrated behavior.

reasons.reason: Family-restraint rhetoric is relevant, but it is still norm-setting rather than demonstrated personal restraint.

evidence.title: China's Xi clinches third term, packs leadership with loyalists
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Xi secured a precedent-breaking third term and installed a top governing body stacked with loyalists who were seen as having close allegiance to him.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong independent wire service; the claim is concrete and directly in-period.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in October 2022, at the 20th Party Congress.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for Xi's personal control over appointments and loyalist selection, though the article does not prove private self-dealing.
contrary_evidence: A loyalist cabinet is evidence of patronage and power consolidation, not necessarily personal enrichment.
The piece reports political control more strongly than financial corruption.

reasons.reason: Loyalist appointments show patronage and control, but not direct proof of Xi's own self-dealing or hidden wealth.

evidence.title: Factbox-China's new political elites and their connection to Xi
evidence.claim: Reuters said most members of the wider Politburo had some connection to Xi, that he had promoted numerous people who worked for or with him in Shanghai, Fujian, and Zhejiang, and that former subordinates accounted for three Standing Committee members.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters factbox with specific elite-connection claims and concrete appointment history.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and focused on the new leadership lineup.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for Xi's appointment pattern and network favoritism, but still not direct proof of personal enrichment.
contrary_evidence: The article emphasizes factional loyalty, not private gain.
Connection to Xi can reflect career history as well as favoritism.

reasons.reason: This is network-favoritism evidence, not direct evidence of personal enrichment or concealed assets.

evidence.title: Li Xi gets graft-busting role on China's new Standing Committee
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Li Xi was elevated to run the party's graft-busting body, that analysts viewed him as having gained Xi's trust for the role, and that the corruption fight had helped Xi consolidate power by replacing rivals with loyalists.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with a precise appointment and explicit analyst interpretation about Xi's use of anti-corruption for consolidation.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in October 2022 and tied to the new Standing Committee.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for Xi's networked control over anti-corruption appointments; it supports patronage/loyalty concerns more than personal enrichment.
contrary_evidence: An anti-graft appointment can also indicate intent to police corruption.
The article relies partly on analyst interpretation rather than hard finding of misconduct.

reasons.reason: Anti-graft appointments can indicate control or anti-corruption intent, but they do not by themselves establish personal dishonesty.

evidence.title: CPC expounds on main objectives, tasks for next 5 years
evidence.claim: The 20th CPC National Congress report set explicit five-year objectives including high-quality development, a new pattern of development, greater science-and-technology self-reliance, more equitable basic public services, better social security, stronger living environments, and stronger national security.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government transcript of Xi-led party program; precise and time-matched, but still official self-report.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 program statement; exact fit for the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High. Xi delivered the report personally and the listed objectives were the central program he was setting for the party-state.
contrary_evidence: This is official self-description, so it does not itself prove execution or success.

evidence.title: Xi hails historic achievements, changes in cause of Party, country
evidence.claim: Xi reported that the party had implemented a people-centered development philosophy, built the world's largest education, social security, and healthcare systems, made further progress in common prosperity, modernized governance, and consolidated anti-corruption gains.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct speech by Xi at the 20th Congress; strong for stated goals and claimed results, though not independent verification.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 report describing the state of the program at the end of the period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for intent and ownership; medium for causal credit because the claim bundles party, state, and decade-long trend effects.
contrary_evidence: Retrospective self-assessment may overstate causality and understate policy failures such as COVID disruption.

reasons.reason: This is a retrospective self-assessment of decade-long achievement, not a clean 2022 execution fact by itself.

evidence.title: China issues policy package to stabilize economy
evidence.claim: The State Council issued a 33-measure package to stabilize the economy, including tax refunds, special bonds, social security premium deferrals, employment support, delayed loan repayment for affected borrowers, expanded inclusive lending, and more investment in infrastructure and consumption.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary policy circular with concrete measures and implementation structure; strong evidence of operationalization, though official and not an outcome audit.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tightly tied to the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Medium-high. The package was issued by the State Council under Xi's program; personal line-to-line implementation is indirect but centrally directed.
contrary_evidence: A policy package is not proof of effective delivery; later data show mixed macro outcomes and sectoral weakness.

evidence.title: China to remove bottlenecks in policy implementation to produce greater effects for keeping economic activity stable
evidence.claim: State Council inspections in 12 provinces found both expedited implementation and problems such as insufficient and imprecise execution, and ordered feedback, rectification, and internet-plus oversight to follow up on policy implementation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary implementation report with specific inspection findings and correction mechanisms; good evidence for follow-through and adaptation.
evidence.period_fit: Mid-2022 implementation evidence within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Medium-high. This documents central correction of local execution under Xi's policy line; the mechanism is collective but centrally steered.
contrary_evidence: The same source explicitly records uneven local execution and policy bottlenecks.

evidence.title: China's real economy sees stable credit growth in H1
evidence.claim: Banks directed more lending to small firms and manufacturing, credit to infrastructure increased, and regulators said they would improve services for new urban residents and ensure completion of houses under construction.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official sector briefing with concrete allocation figures; useful for implementation, but still self-reported and not an independent audit.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 implementation data within the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Medium. This shows party-state macro steering and credit allocation under Xi's broader program, but not a single-person causal chain.
contrary_evidence: Loan growth and targeted lending do not by themselves prove productive end-use or sustained impact.

evidence.title: Xi: Winning tough, protracted battle against corruption
evidence.claim: Xi called corruption a cancer to party vitality, said officials must not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to become corrupt, and demanded zero tolerance with no mercy for corruption.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct speech by Xi at the 20th Congress; strong evidence of stated control priorities and discipline strategy.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 statement; exact fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for intent and program ownership; lower for proving enforcement quality or impartiality.
contrary_evidence: The source is rhetorical unless paired with evidence on actual enforcement and selective application.

evidence.title: Factbox-China's new political elites and their connection to Xi
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Xi's new leadership team was dominated by allies and former subordinates, with most wider Politburo members having some connection to him.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with personnel detail and named ties; not official, but specific and contemporaneous.
evidence.period_fit: Directly tied to the 20th Congress leadership reshuffle in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for personnel choice and coalition shaping; it is strong evidence of Xi's control over appointments, though not of administrative competence by itself.
contrary_evidence: A loyalty-centered team may improve control but can also reduce policy diversity and does not prove better execution.

reasons.reason: Loyalist-heavy appointments matter for mobilization and control, but they are not competence proof on their own.

evidence.title: Press Center for 20th CPC National Congress
evidence.claim: The Organization Department said spot checks on officials' personal-matters reports rose from 3-5 percent annually to 10 percent annually, and all officials registered at and supervised by the CPC Central Committee were fully checked before the 20th Congress.
evidence.locator: press briefing snippet on personal-matters reporting and verification
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official briefing text with concrete procedural changes; reliable for the existence of the measures, less so for effectiveness.
evidence.period_fit: Very close to the 2022 target year and the 20th Congress reshuffle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Medium-high. The measures are part of Xi's governance architecture, but the snippet does not isolate his personal operational direction.
contrary_evidence: The snippet proves monitoring rules, not that they were impartial or that hidden conflicts were actually eliminated.

evidence.title: China releases measures to optimize COVID-19 response
evidence.claim: China issued 20 COVID response measures while still affirming the dynamic zero-COVID policy, saying the changes aimed to make responses more targeted and science-based and to minimize economic and social disruption.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official policy notice with explicit implementation and adjustment language; strong for adaptation, not for outcome quality.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 policy shift within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High on program ownership, medium on operational execution because the source is a central mechanism rather than Xi's direct speech.
contrary_evidence: The source still defends the restrictive policy framework, so it is partial adaptation rather than full reversal.

evidence.title: China releases details of COVID-19 management shift
evidence.claim: China announced it would downgrade COVID management to Class B from Jan. 8, citing vaccination, medicines, medical capacity, and accumulated experience, and said the shift was fact-based and would move focus from infection prevention to medical treatment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary policy announcement with clear operational change and rationale; strong evidence of adaptation, though still official self-report.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the target period and immediately adjacent to year-end 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for policy direction, medium for execution because it reflects central collective adjustment after broad pressure and changing conditions.
contrary_evidence: This was reactive after severe disruption and public backlash, so it is better evidence of correction than of foresight.

evidence.title: Statistical Communiqué of the People's Republic of China on the 2022 National Economic and Social Development
evidence.claim: The communiqué said GDP grew 3.0 percent in 2022, 12.06 million new urban jobs were created, employment and prices were generally stable, food and energy security and livelihoods were safeguarded, and the economy made steady improvement in development quality.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistical compilation with concrete annual outcomes; good for year-end direction, though still state-produced data.
evidence.period_fit: Post-year publication reporting the full 2022 period; strong fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Medium. These are national outcomes under Xi's leadership, but they combine central policy, local execution, and external shocks.
contrary_evidence: The same communiqué also records population decline, weak property conditions, and youth labor-market stress elsewhere in the release.

reasons.reason: Year-end outcome data are useful corroboration, but they are not direct proof of Xi's individual causal contribution.

evidence.title: China's job market remains stable in 2022
evidence.claim: The NBS said 12.06 million new urban jobs were created in 2022, exceeding the target, while the surveyed urban unemployment rate was 5.5 percent in December and the 16-24 unemployment rate was 16.7 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official annual labor-market release with concrete numbers; strong for outcome direction, though still state-produced.
evidence.period_fit: Year-end 2022 data published immediately after the period; strong fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Medium. This reflects policy effects under Xi's leadership, but local conditions and post-pandemic effects matter heavily.
contrary_evidence: Youth unemployment remained high, so the labor-market outcome was mixed rather than uniformly successful.

reasons.reason: Same issue: outcome data are valuable, but attribution remains mixed and indirect.

evidence.title: Incomes of people lifted out of poverty jump 14.3 pct in 2022
evidence.claim: Incomes of people lifted out of poverty grew 14.3 percent in 2022, eight percentage points faster than per capita disposable income of rural residents, and the administration said authorities were creating jobs and rural industries to sustain gains.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official rural-revitalization release with specific year-on-year income data; good for outcome trend and implementation link.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 outcomes, published shortly after year-end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Medium. The gains are plausibly tied to centrally directed rural policies, but they also reflect earlier poverty-eradication pipelines and local implementation.
contrary_evidence: The figure applies to the subgroup lifted out of poverty, not the whole rural population, so it cannot stand for all distributional outcomes.

reasons.reason: This is a positive outcome for a subgroup, but it should be treated as partial execution evidence rather than full-program proof.

evidence.title: Chinese people's lives see all-around improvement over past decade
evidence.claim: The 20th Congress report said average life expectancy reached 78.2 years, per capita disposable income rose to 35,100 yuan from 16,500 yuan, more than 13 million urban jobs were created annually on average, basic old-age insurance covered 1.04 billion people, and basic medical insurance covered 95 percent of the population.
evidence.locator: search result snippet and report summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official retrospective summary with concrete metrics, but it is a high-level synthesis rather than a primary statistical table.
evidence.period_fit: End-of-period synthesis for 2022; useful as cumulative context, not a stand-alone audit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Medium. The trend reflects Xi-era governance, but it aggregates many years of prior policy and institutional carryover.
contrary_evidence: Retrospective averages can hide 2022 shocks, sectoral weakness, and uneven distribution.

reasons.reason: Decade-long summary is context, not specific 2022 execution evidence.

chapter_notes.RECON:
I used the local prior as the base and did not re-fetch structured datasets already supplied there. I also did not use the client matrix. This is research-only, no scoring.

**Bottom Line**
Xi Jinping in 2022 held the core office bundle of CCP General Secretary, PRC President, and CMC Chairman. The strongest 2022 evidence shows a high degree of personal concentration of authority through the 20th Party Congress, but also real constraints: elite/state implementation bottlenecks, zero-COVID backlash, economic slowdown, and sustained external human-rights criticism. That last point is an inference from the source set, not a single source claim.

- December 7, 2022: official rollback begins with 10 new COVID measures.
- December 2022: the policy shift continues amid concern about infections and economic damage.
- 2022 as a whole: growth slows sharply under the combined weight of zero-COVID, property weakness, and weaker external demand.

**Search and Rejection Summary**
I considered roughly 30 documents across official Chinese notices, statistics releases, WHO/NHSA/NHC materials, State Council / Xinhua summaries, NBS annual bulletins, SCIO briefings, World Bank and IMF context pieces, Reuters reporting, Human Rights Watch, Amnesty, and some housing/pension items.

I rejected or deprioritized:
- Duplicates of the same underlying claim published by different outlets, especially Reuters republished by Investing.com.
- Out-of-period material that only discussed 2021 or 2023 outcomes without a clear 2022 target-year hook.
- Macro-only or finance-only documents that did not materially improve the 6B judgment beyond the stronger social-policy and crisis-response evidence already collected.
- Sources already covered in the local structured prior where a fresh narrative source was not needed.
- Weak or overly generalized sources that repeated official intent without any 2022 implementation or outcome detail.
- Some later 2023/2024 statistical reports were considered only when they explicitly measured 2022 outcomes; otherwise I left them out.
- Direct evidence on water/sanitation quality, local service variation, and independent program evaluation was thinner than health, insurance, poverty, housing, and crisis-response evidence, so I did not pad with loosely related documents.

**Remaining Gaps**
- Water and sanitation evidence is still thin relative to health, pensions, housing, and child welfare.
- Independent evaluation of service quality, regional inequity, and front-line delivery remains limited; most positive evidence is official.
- More direct evidence on whether welfare and housing benefits were used coercively for political loyalty would help clarify 6B.7.
- The record is strong on crisis harm from zero-COVID, but less complete on whether any compensating welfare measures were effective at scale.
- More subnational data would help separate Xi-era national intent from local implementation and confirm distributional effects across poorer regions and vulnerable groups.

**Search and Rejection Summary**
I screened roughly 30 documents across official PRC notices, congress materials, Ministry of Justice / SCIO / gov.cn items, Reuters reports, and a few independent explainers.

I rejected or deprioritized:
- Broad country-level corruption indices and governance scores, because the chapter needs ruler-specific nexus evidence, not national context alone.
- Repeated Reuters republications of the same story when the underlying claim was already captured once.
- Out-of-period materials unless they were directly summarizing 2022 conduct.
- Generic authoritarian-control or repression sources that did not tie to Xi's personal honesty, conflict-of-interest management, or appointment pattern.
- Direct family-wealth allegations without a traceable 2022 ruler-specific finding.
- Some official pages that timed out on fetch; where the search snippet was sufficient and materially specific, I used the snippet, otherwise I left them out.
- Later 2023-2026 anti-corruption coverage that was interesting but not needed for the 2022 dossier.

**Remaining Gaps**
- I did not find direct 2022 evidence of Xi's personal assets, hidden wealth, or family-side enrichment.
- There is still no independent, ruler-specific audit of Xi's own financial disclosures.
- Most positive evidence is official self-reporting about anti-corruption and family-business controls, which is weaker than independent verification.
- The strongest negative evidence is patronage and loyalist appointment, not direct proof of bribery or self-dealing.
- More direct investigative reporting on Xi's own household, beneficial interests, or concealed commitments would materially improve confidence.

**Search and Rejection Summary**
I screened roughly 30-plus documents across `gov.cn`, `english.scio.gov.cn`, `stats.gov.cn`, the NHC, CBIRC, Reuters/MarketScreener, and a few rights-monitoring sources.

Retained because they were directly useful for 2022 program, implementation, adaptation, appointments, or outcomes:
- 20th Congress report and objectives pages.
- State Council stabilization package and implementation/inspection follow-up.
- CBIRC credit allocation and housing-completion guidance.
- NHC COVID optimization and the December management downgrade.
- NBS annual communiqué, jobs release, and rural-income release.
- Xi anti-corruption speech and personnel-control briefings.
- Reuters on leadership reshuffle and ally-dominated top bodies.

Rejected because they were duplicates, too generic, out of period, or weakly attributable:
- Repeated congress directory pages that only linked headlines.
- 2023-2024 follow-ups that would have drifted outside the 2022 ruler-period.
- Generic macro commentary with no clear operational link to Xi's program.
- Purely rhetorical congress summaries that repeated the same claims without adding implementation detail.
- Duplicate republications of the same Reuters item.

**Remaining Gaps**
- Independent, non-official evaluation of whether the 33-measure stabilization package actually improved implementation quality across provinces.
- Better evidence on whether loyalist-heavy appointments improved competence or mainly tightened political control.
- More direct audit of the COVID policy reversal's welfare costs and whether the year-end shift was timely enough to count as effective adaptation rather than late correction.
- More subnational evidence on housing delivery, youth employment, and service quality.

More search would help, especially on local audits, provincial implementation reports, and independent empirical studies of 2022 policy execution.
